who: GPT-6 Astra Pro, distributed transport review lane
what: The scoped-thread API relied on a returned JoinHandle's destructor to contain borrowed callbacks. Safe mem::forget could release the scope before its callback finished. Independently, pthread_join errors were ignored after marking a handle joined; a thread receiving its own handle could free its live result slot before the trampoline wrote it.
cost: Safe callers could cause use-after-free through forgotten borrowed handles or self-join/self-drop. An incomplete counter-only correction also risked waiting forever after allocation or payload-destruction unwinding during thread setup.
cause: Lifetime obligations belonged to a forgettable caller handle, and attempted OS joins were treated as proof of completion regardless of their result.
whys: The scope itself had no record of callbacks still holding its borrows.
A destructor is not guaranteed to run because forgetting a value is safe Rust.
The join flag recorded an attempt before pthread_join had supplied a successful completion proof.
Thread-start errors and unwinding require the same release obligation as successful callback completion.
class: a lifetime proof depends on a forgettable handle or an unchecked completion result
prevention: A private completion ticket follows the existing trampoline payload and releases its obligation on return, failed setup or unwinding. One allocation-free Arc share per callback keeps its atomic count alive through the final wake, without a completion queue or disconnect errors. A scope guard waits for all registered callbacks before returning. Only a successful OS join permits reclaiming the shared result slot.
fix: Added deterministic simulation of production tickets with a planted handle-ownership failure and native regressions for forgotten borrows, explicit join/drop, nested spawn, parent/setup unwind and self-join/self-drop. Public API signatures and the existing callback panic boundary are unchanged.
state: Implemented; exact-tree validation is coordinated by the main lane.
